name: Spar
description: Spar is the most popular card game in Ghana. It is a trick-taking game without trumps in which the object is to win the last trick. Played by 2 to 4 players (up to 7 possible) with 35 cards from a standard pack. Similar games are played in Benin as Jeu de Carte and in Togo as Sipa. Often played for money or for enjoyment.
deck: 35 cards from a standard 52-card pack: each suit has 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A (Ace high). The Ace of Spades is normally not used, so the highest spade is the King.

history.origins: Likely introduced by European sailors playing Whist or similar games, adapted locally.
timeline: 1900s: Becomes a staple in Ghanaian communities.
history.cultural: Often played with much banter and slapping of cards.
history.evolution: The emphasis on the 'last trick' is a hallmark of many African trick games.

setup.deck: 35 cards: 6 through Ace in each suit; Ace of Spades normally not used.
setup.dealing: First dealer chosen at random; thereafter the winner of each hand deals the next. Five cards to each player: a batch of three to each (starting with player to dealer's left if clockwise), then a batch of two each, ending with the dealer.

rules.objective: The object is to win the last (fifth) trick of each hand. There are no trumps. The player who wins the last trick scores points: 3 if the winning card is a 6, 2 if a 7, and 1 if 8 or higher. The session continues for as long as players wish with no fixed target score.
rules.gameplay: Player to dealer's left leads any card. Others must follow suit if possible; if not, any card. Highest card of the suit led wins the trick. Cards stay in a face-up pile. Trick winner leads to the next trick. Five tricks per hand. Winner of the last trick scores: 3 points if winning card is a 6, 2 if a 7, 1 if 8 or higher. Winner of the hand deals the next hand.
keyRules: Must follow suit if possible; otherwise any card.
Highest card of led suit wins the trick.
Winner of the last trick scores 3 (with 6), 2 (with 7), or 1 (with 8 or higher) point(s).
Winner of the hand deals next; no fixed target score, session continues as players wish.

strategy.basic: Save your high cards (Aces/Kings) for the end. Winning the last trick is crucial. Don't waste an Ace early on a trick worth nothing.
strategy.intermediate: Counting Suits: Since the deck is small, knowing when a suit is exhausted is easy. Lead a long suit to force opponents to discard their high cards in other suits.
strategy.advanced: The 'Spar' Bluff: Pretend to be weak to induce a lead, then slam your Ace down on the last trick.
tips: Winning the last trick with a 6 scores 3 points; with a 7 scores 2; with 8 or higher scores 1.
Lead to force opponents to spend high cards when you cannot win the trick.

scoring.description: Winner of the last trick scores: 3 points if the winning card is a 6, 2 if a 7, 1 if 8 or higher. No fixed target; session continues as players wish. When played for money, winner is paid 1, 2 or 3 stakes by each other player.
scoring.winCondition: Win the last (fifth) trick; score 3, 2 or 1 point depending on the winning card (6, 7, or 8+).
